Solve a model with guided perfect foresight

Source: R/solve_guided.R
solve_guided.Rd

Reaches a full-horizon solution by solving cheap endpoint problems first and using their capacity as targets for the expensive full solve. Unlike solve_recursive(), every subproblem sees the horizon's last milestone, so the transition is disciplined by where it must arrive rather than by local optimality — and the final stage is one ordinary full-horizon solve, whose objective is therefore directly comparable to a true perfect-foresight one.

Usage

solve_guided(
  object,
  name = NULL,
  ...,
  horizon = NULL,
  stages = c("endpoint", "pairs", "final"),
  slack = 0.2,
  basis = c("cap", "ncap"),
  mode = c("lo", "fx"),
  calendar_guide = NULL,
  direction = c("backward", "forward"),
  solver = NULL,
  on_infeasible = c("relax", "stop"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  keep_scenarios = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

a model object.

name

character, the sequence name (a scenario folder).

...

passed to interpolate_model() for every stage.

horizon

a horizon; defaults to the model's own. At least two milestone years are required.

stages

character, which stages to run, in order. Defaults to c("endpoint", "pairs", "final"); add "base" and/or "transition".

slack

numeric in [0, 1], how far below a target the solver may go (the bound is (1 - slack) * target). 0.2 by default.

basis

"cap" (default) or "ncap" — see Details.

mode

"lo" (default) writes lower bounds; "fx" fixes capacity.

calendar_guide

an optional reduced newCalendar() used for the guide stages (base, endpoint, transition, pairs) but never for final.

direction

"backward" (default) or "forward", for the pairs stage.

solver

a solver option list; the scenario's default when NULL.

on_infeasible

"relax" (default) retries a stage with progressively looser guidance before giving up; "stop" fails immediately.

overwrite

logical; FALSE (default) refuses to run when a variant of the same label already exists on disk with a different type or different parameters. TRUE skips that guard and writes into it.

keep_scenarios

logical, keep each stage's scenario object in the result.

verbose

logical.

Value

a guided object: stages (a tibble of what ran), scenarios, targets, ledger, and final — the full-horizon solved scenario.

Details

Stages, each stored as an own-problem variant of one scenario:

  • "base" — solve the base year alone and write the result back as stock, so the past enters later stages as sunk capacity rather than being re-optimised.

  • "endpoint" — solve {base, last}. Whatever survives from the base year stands; everything else is built at the last milestone. This is the end-state fleet. The base-year row is kept so discounting stays anchored there.

  • "transition" — optionally carry the endpoint target across every milestone on a reduced calendar_guide, cheaply.

  • "pairs" — refine each interior milestone against the endpoint, via guided_windows().

  • "final" — the deliverable: the full horizon with every accumulated target imposed as a bound.

Targets bound the STANDING FLEET (cap.lo) by default. basis = "ncap" bounds the build rate instead and divides by the period length, because ncap.* bounds are multiplied by pPeriodLen in the equations while the solved variable is already an annual rate.

See also

solve_recursive(), apply_targets(), guided_gap()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
open_project(tempdir())

ek  <- topia$modules$electricity$R3
mod <- newModel("TOPIA", data = ek$repo,
                calendar = topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24,
                region = ek$regions,
                horizon = topia$modules$horizons$base,
                discount = 0.05)
mod <- setGeoscale(mod, ek$geoscale)

# the endpoint first, then each neighbouring pair, then the full horizon
# with the guidance as bounds
res <- solve_guided(mod, name = "GUIDED", slack = 0.2,
                    solver = solver_options$glpk)
sum(getData(res$final, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)$value)
} # }
